proposedOperatorData.shortDescription: Cardiff International White Water (CIWW) is the UK's first on-demand white water centre, set on Cardiff Bay's waterfront. Opened in 2010, it offers white water rafting, kayaking, SUP, indoor surfing, and climbing for all ages from 6+, hosted on an Olympic-specification 258-metre artificial river course.
proposedOperatorData.shortDescriptionNote: Drafted from verified Wikipedia and official website content. Needs editorial review before publishing.
proposedOperatorData.fullDescription:
Cardiff International White Water (CIWW) is the United Kingdom's first on-demand white water facility, situated within the International Sports Village on the shores of Cardiff Bay. Opened on 26 March 2010, the centre was built at a cost of £13.3 million — funded by the Welsh Assembly Government, Sportlot, the Welsh Canoe Association, and the Heritage Lottery Fund — and was designed by French specialist firm HydroStadium, the same company behind the Olympic white water venues at Sydney, Athens, and Beijing.

The course runs 258 metres, drops 3.9 metres, and generates a flow of up to 10 m³/s at competition grade. In June 2012, CIWW hosted the opening round of the ICF Canoe Slalom World Cup, which international athletes used as a final selection event for the 2012 London Olympics.

Visitors can choose from three broad activity categories: Thrills and Spills (white water rafting, tubing, mini rafts, hot dogging), Calm and Collected (SUP taster, SUP yoga, gorge walking, kayaking courses), and High and Dry (climbing wall, indoor wave body-boarding, indoor Flowrider stand-up surfing). All activities are available from age 6. The centre also runs the CIWW Kids Academy, corporate team building, and first aid training.

CIWW is accredited by Adventure Smart UK, affiliated with the International Rafting Federation (IRF), and holds ShOut2 membership. With a TripAdvisor rating of 4.9/5 from over 1,500 reviews and ranked #1 of all Tours and Activities in Cardiff, it is one of Wales's most celebrated adventure venues.
proposedOperatorData.fullDescriptionNote: Drafted from Wikipedia, the operator website, and VisitWales listing. The 'Olympic venue' framing should be used with care — CIWW is Olympic-grade and hosted ICF World Cup qualification events, but the 2012 Olympics white water events were held at Lee Valley (Hertfordshire), not Cardiff. Needs editorial review before publishing.

history.designerNote: HydroStadium also designed the Olympic white water venues at Sydney 2000, Athens 2004, and Beijing 2008.
history.olympicConnectionNote: CIWW is NOT a 2012 Olympic venue — the London 2012 canoe slalom events were held at Lee Valley White Water Centre, Hertfordshire. However, CIWW hosted the ICF Canoe Slalom World Cup Round 1 (8–10 June 2012), which nations used as a final athlete selection event for London 2012. CIWW is built to Olympic competition specification by the same designers. The 'Olympic legacy' framing is accurate only in this qualified sense — editors should not describe it as a '2012 Olympic venue'.

claimsNeedingHumanReview.issue: CIWW is frequently described informally as an 'Olympic venue' or 'built for the Olympics', but this is misleading. The 2012 London Olympics white water events were held at Lee Valley White Water Centre (Hertfordshire). CIWW is Olympic-specification (designed by HydroStadium, same as Sydney/Athens/Beijing Olympic courses) and hosted an ICF World Cup qualifying event in June 2012 used for Olympic athlete selection — but it was not itself a 2012 Games venue.
claimsNeedingHumanReview.action: If the description refers to Olympics, use the qualified framing: 'Olympic-specification course, designed by HydroStadium (designers of the Sydney, Athens, and Beijing Olympic courses)' or 'hosted ICF World Cup events used for 2012 London Olympics athlete selection'. Do not describe it as 'the Olympic white water venue' or 'built for the Olympics'.
